title: one line of .respawnpack/ops-log.jsonl - an append-only operations-log row (G17, decision 50)
description: ⛔ APPEND-ONLY AND MACHINE-LOCAL. The ops log is the single owner of what an operation DID and how it turned out (the memo's single-sourcing rule): a decision, a candidate claim or CONTINUITY's note may point at a row by its `digest`, none may restate its `result`. One JSON object per line, written only through core/_io.js appendLine (ordering and torn-tail detection, NOT atomicity) by the `log` verb and the savepoint, read only through readLinesClassified. The file lives under .respawnpack/, which the installer gitignores, so it NEVER travels in a clone (durability class `runtime`). Each row seals the one before it: `digest` is core/_io.js canonicalDigest of the row WITHOUT its own `digest` field, and `prevDigest` is the previous row's `digest` (null on the first row), so a rewritten or spliced earlier row breaks the chain and is refused. The disclosed limit: a rewrite of the LAST row that also recomputes its own digest is not detectable by the chain alone until the next row (the savepoint's, every write) seals it.

by.description: Who did it - required and non-empty (G6's rule: an action with no author is refused before anything is written). `savepoint` for the savepoint's own row.

action.description: What was done, one line (refused over 1,000 characters or spanning lines).

result.description: The outcome, one line. The savepoint's row records the rollup the run exits with.

refs.description: Ids this action points at (an incident id, a prior row's digest, a write cycle) - pointers, never restated bodies.

cycleId.description: The source revision resolved the way the savepoint resolves it (state.sourceRevision, or 'no-revision').

prevDigest.description: The previous row's `digest`; null on the first row.

digest.description: canonicalDigest of this row with its own `digest` field removed - what the next row's prevDigest seals.
